item.title: Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina plans Bangladesh return: 'I may be killed, I may be sent to prison'
item.description: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh by December. She is prepared to face arrest, imprisonment, or even execution upon her arrival. Hasina fled the country in August 2024 after widespread protests ended her rule. Her party faces repression and legal proceedings following the change in government.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: China lost more than 50% of its mangrove forests by the 2000s, now it has restored 22,500 hectares of the trees
item.description: China has made remarkable strides in restoring its mangrove ecosystems, committing to large-scale projects that have expanded coverage significantly. By planting and revitalizing thousands of hectares, not only has biodiversity surged, but the quality of these crucial habitats has also seen improvement. Robust legal measures now safeguard more than ninety percent of mangrove areas, complemented by the establishment of an international center focused on mangrove conservation in Shenzhen.

item.title: Antarctica averages minus 55°C at Vostok Station, yet a lake remains liquid beneath four kilometres of ice
item.description: Lake Vostok, a massive body of water, lies four kilometers beneath Antarctic ice. This subglacial lake remains liquid due to insulating ice and geothermal heat. Its existence challenges our understanding of life's extreme limits and nature's magic. The lake has been isolated from the atmosphere for millions of years. Scientists continue to study this unique environment and its potential inhabitants.

item.title: Trump bans new Chinese robots and power inverters over security fears
item.description: Explaining the decision, the FCC said the targeted products could expose the country to supply chain risks and cyber threats. "These devices could create supply chain vulnerabilities that could disrupt US economic and national security and could create a cybersecurity risk that threatened American critical infrastructure," the agency said. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr added, "The FCC will continue to do our part to secure America’s critical supply chains."

item.title: Middle East war escalates: Multiple dead in US-Saudi strikes in Iraq; Iran targets Hormuz ships - top developments
item.description: United States and Saudi Arabia launched joint strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq. Iran claimed to have intercepted oil tankers and fired missiles at US installations. Eight Iraqi PMF members were killed in the joint US-Saudi attacks. Oil prices climbed amid concerns over energy supply disruptions. Diplomatic efforts continue as tensions between nations rise.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Singapore built a floating solar farm in the sea, but thousands of barnacles turned it into an engineering challenge that could sink its 13,000 solar panels
item.description: Singapore uses floating solar farms to overcome land scarcity for renewable energy goals. Marine organisms like barnacles attach to pontoons, adding significant weight and reducing buoyancy. This biofouling accelerates corrosion and can damage electrical components of the solar arrays. Maintaining these offshore solar plants requires constant maintenance and inspections.

item.title: Shark attack rescuer Charlie Verco breaks world paddleboarding record
item.description: Australian paddleboarder Charlie Verco won his fourth Molokai to Oahu world championship in Hawaii in record time, just weeks after rescuing a woman during a great white shark attack off Sydney's Coogee Beach. The trained surf lifesaver said a relaxed approach helped him break the previous course record by three minutes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Oman proposes Gulf-backed voluntary fees to use Hormuz
item.description: Oman has presented Iran with a plan backed by Gulf states for managing the Strait of Hormuz. This proposal includes collecting voluntary fees for ships utilizing the vital waterway. Iran has yet to respond to the Omani proposals for trade disruption resolution. The plan aims to avoid sole Iranian control and make fees voluntary. Gulf Cooperation Council ministers met to discuss waterway safety and cooperation.

item.title: Italy's fertility rate falls to 80-year low: Report
item.description: Italy's birth rate fell nearly four percent last year, reaching a historic low. The fertility rate dropped to 1.14 children per woman, a significant decline. Economic pressures and a lack of support for working mothers contributed to this trend. This rate is far below the 2.1 needed for a stable population. Motherhood desires clash with job insecurity and high living costs.

item.title: New chapter in reading: AI companion tools let readers chat with books
item.description: New artificial intelligence tools now let readers ask questions directly to books. These innovative platforms offer e-books and audiobooks alongside AI chatbots for immediate answers. Companies like Sinai.ai and Amazon's Audible are developing these interactive reading experiences. However, copyright and author compensation remain significant unresolved issues for these tools. Some platforms are exploring ways to pay authors and publishers for their content.

item.title: US envoy Gor to visit Bangladesh as Dhaka deepens ties with Beijing
item.description: US special envoy Sergio Gor will visit Bangladesh on July 30. He will meet Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and the foreign minister. This visit follows Prime Minister Rahman's recent tour of China. The US seeks understanding of Bangladesh's foreign policy priorities. Washington remains concerned over China's economic corridor proposal.
item.dc:creator: Ahsan Tasnim

item.title: What happened to Yonna? Twitch streamer reacts after e-bike accident on livestream
item.description: Twitch streamer and TikTok creator Yonna crashed an e-bike during a recent IRL livestream after losing control and hitting a gate. She first answered “No” when friends asked if she was okay but later laughed and joked about the incident. No serious injury has been confirmed. Yonna recently returned to Kai Cenat’s Streamer University 2026 as Drama Club director.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Kai Cenat defends Tyla from alleged catcaller during Disney World livestream, fans applaud response
item.description: Twitch streamer Kai Cenat defended singer Tyla from a man during a Disney World livestream. He confronted the individual who was allegedly shouting at the singer. The brief exchange was captured on the livestream and quickly went viral online. Fans praised Kai for his respectful and mature handling of the uncomfortable situation. The livestream also marked the reunion of Kai and Tyla after nearly two years.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Twitch streamer NateDeBaiits heartbroken after fatal California birthday party shooting claims friend's life
item.description: A birthday party for Twitch streamer NateDeBaiits tragically ended with a shooting. One person died and six others sustained injuries during the California event. The deceased was identified as Desiderio Romero V, a close friend of the streamer. Police are investigating the incident which occurred after a fight broke out. No arrests have been made as authorities review evidence.
